question: Which of these is NOT among the four code structures?

answers.feedback: No! Methods are among the most prevalent structures, especially when you are dealing with lists/arrays and tables.

question: What is the main danger behind giving variables the same names as function/method names?

answers.answer: Python will mix up the variable and the function/method, and you won't be able to use the function/method anymore.
answers.feedback: Yes! Any further attempts to use the function/method will instead be interpreted as using the variable.

answers.answer: You will be liable to confuse the function/method and the variable.
answers.feedback: No! While this is certainly a possibility, this is not the main hazard.

answers.answer: Python will crash and all the servers will shut down
answers.feedback: No! The server will run as normal, just with an overridden function/method name. You can reset by simply restarting the Kernel.
